content.comment_body: Hello, I'm a beginner trying to connect to a [product_name]. Here are my network settings: [product_name] - IP: 192.168.0.2, Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0, Gateway: 192.168.0.0. My PC - IP: 192.168.0.1, Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0, Gateway: 192.168.0.0. Although my PC shows the status as online, I'm unable to connect and an error appears (see attachment). Can anyone assist?
Are you connecting your PC directly to the [product_name] or is there a router involved?
It's a direct connection to the [product_name].
Is there anyone who can provide some help?
Which operating system are you using? Also, which [product_name] software version are you working with? If there's no router present, setting a gateway IP might not be necessary.
I'm using Windows XP and [product_name] software version [version_no]. I'll try removing the gateway setting.
In the German section of the forum, a user faced a similar issue with Windows 8. There, the problem was due to an outdated network card driver.
I considered this but wasn't certain. Thank you—I'll check the drivers!

Hi! Has anyone found a workaround for this problem? I'm experiencing the same issue—I tried [product_name] software version [version_no] on multiple PCs (Windows XP, Windows 7, Windows 8, including virtual machines) but nothing helped. Now I’m unsure if the problem is just the network adapter driver.
Hello everyone. I've encountered this problem several times. Occasionally, it's due to a Wi-Fi connection, a faulty patch cord, or differing IP addresses set in the project.

Hi all, I've finally found a solution! The issue truly was with the network adapter drivers, as mentioned by others in this thread. On my test PCs, the operating systems used default drivers right after installation. Due to Russian localization, the ethernet network adapter's name in Device Manager showed Cyrillic characters (see attachment). After updating the driver so the adapter's name appeared only in English, communication with the [product_name] worked perfectly. This solution also helped in virtual systems—make sure both host and virtual adapter names have no non-English symbols.
Thank you for sharing your helpful feedback.
Yes, that's true. In my situation, disabling and then enabling the network adapter made it work.
Is the [product_name] IP address reachable via ping?
Yes, it is pingable. Why do you ask?

Thank you for the information. I spent about 8 hours checking IP addresses, cables, and the computer itself. The problem turned out to be the driver with Cyrillic characters. I downloaded a version for my computer (even though there was no new version available), installed it, and it resolved the issue. Best regards for your advice.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing ongoing difficulties connecting their PCs to the [product_name] using [product_name] software version [version_no]. Multiple troubleshooting steps have been attempted, including network setting adjustments, driver updates, trying different PCs and operating system versions, but the solution was not evident. The unclear error causes—such as network adapter drivers, cabling problems, or mismatched IP settings—contribute to user uncertainty and frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a simple and dependable process for establishing a connection between the PC and the [product_name] using [product_name] software, along with clear troubleshooting instructions and informative error messages if issues occur.
